- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 82, adjust downward by 1–2% per period unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 forecasts.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 prices as baseline for correction.
